articleTitle: Effect of Growth Temperature on Structures and Magnetoresistive Properties of Fe/Cr Multilayers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe/Cr multilayer films, [Fe (21Å)-Cr (13Å)]×30, were deposited on MgO (100) single crystal and glass substrates by vacuum evaporation, with the substrate temperature varied. The resistivity under zero field was smallest, and the magnetic contribution was largest, for samples prepared with the substrate temperature between 150°C and 200°C, which accordingly exhibited the largest magnetoresistive change below 3 kOe (6% at room temperature, 20% at 77K).

articleTitle: Grain Diameter and Magnetic Properties of Rapidly Quenched Fe-M-Si-Ge (M=Ti, V, Zr, Nb, Ta) and Fe-Hf-Cu Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The grain diameters and magnetic properties of rapidly quenched Fe-M-Si-Ge (M=Ti, V, Zr, Nb, Ta) and Fe-Hf-Cu alloy ribbons were investigated. The grain size of Fe-Ta-Si-Ge alloys decreases rapidly from 2700 Å to about 400 Å with the addition of up to 3 at% Ta. The coercivity increases rapidly from 2.3 to 30 Oe with increasing Ta content. For the Fe-M-Si-Ge alloy systems, the decrease in grain diameter and increase in coercivity with the addition of M rank in the order Ta, Nb, Zr, Ti, V. The grain diameter of Fe-Hf-Cu alloys decreases to about 600 Å as the Hf content is increased to 4 to 6 at%. The coercivity increases to about 20 Oe with increasing Hf content. The coercivity of these rapidly quenched Fe-base alloys is roughly proportional to the reciprocal of the grain diameter.

articleTitle: Effect of Magnetic Field on Magnetic Anisotropy Sensor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Nondestructive methods for measurement of mechanical stress are important to studies of magnetic materials. Magnetic anisotropy sensors (MAS), which have been employed in stress and torque sensors, can also be utilized in the noncontact detection of magnetic anisotropy in materials to estimate stress or defects in them. However, because MAS is a probe type sensor, it is affected by external magnetic fields, a serious drawback to practical use. This paper discusses the effect of external magnetic fields on MAS's and proposes a method to reduce their influence.

articleTitle: Conversion Theory of Magnetic Anisotropy Sensor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A magnetic anisotropy sensor (MAS) enables the noncontact measurement of mechanical stress in ferromagnetic materials. This paper deals with the conversion theory of the MAS output voltage, utilizing a directional permeability distribution which assumes an elliptical form in the specimen. The relative permeability is proportional to the stress, and the theoretical expression for the output voltage is derived from the concept of a directional permeability distribution. The calculated values for the output voltage are comparatively close to measured values due to changes in stress.

articleTitle: Fundamental Characteristics of Differential Transformer Type Displacement Sensor Using a YBCO Superconductor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A displacement sensor was constructed using a YBCO superconductor. The sensor consisted of an excitation coil, a differential coil, and a superconducting YBCO rod. The inductance of the differential coil decreased as a result of perfect diamagnetism (the Meissner effect) when the YBCO rod entered the coil. The YBCO rod could be shifted by as much as ±12 mm in the center of the differential coil, along the axis of the rod, by moving the holder attached to the rod. The relationship between the output voltage of the differential coil and the displacement of the rod was measured using a lock-in amplifier. Experimental results indicate that the displacement sensor characteristics, including sensitivity, linearity, stability, frequency dependence, and absence of hysteresis, are satisfactory. Together with the above results, the electrical properties of the superconducting materials were also examined and compared with those of ferrite and soft iron.

articleTitle: Anisotropy of Microcrystalline Co-Nb-Zr-N Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Field-induced anisotropy in Co-Nb-Zr-N soft magnetic thin films with 9 at% nitrogen was investigated. Samples were prepared by ion beam sputtering in Ar+N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. After pre-annealing for 1 hour at 600 °C, reversible relaxation of the field-induced anisotropy was observed, with ΔK<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ux</sub>=700 to 1500 J/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The dependences of the anisotropy on annealing temperature T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ra</inf> and annealing time t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ra</sub> were studied.

articleTitle: Effect of Heat-Treatment on the Magnetic Properties and Microstructure of Electroless-Plated CoNiP Films for Perpendicular Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of heat treatment on the magnetic properties and microstructure of electroless plated CoNiP films for use as perpendicular magnetic recording media was investigated, in order to clarify the film microstructure in the as deposited state, as well as to evaluate their thermal stability. The as-deposited film consisted of a mixture of ≪002≫ perpendicularly oriented hep structure, and fcc structure without any obvious crystal orientation. Heat treatment at temperatures above 400°C changed the dominant crystal structure from hep to fcc. The crystallites grow larger with heat treatment, causing a sharp change in magnetic properties. These changes were due to the disappearance of the magnetocrystalline anisotropy induced by the cobalt hep structure, and the decrease in the shape magnetic anisotropy due to the change in film topology. On the basis of these results, it is suggested that a compositional inhomogeneity due to the segregation of Co-rich regions exists in the as-deposited films; this segregation disappears with heat treatment at higher temperature, so that the crystal structure of the film changes to an fcc structure.

articleTitle: Dynamic Response Analysis of Linear Pulse Motor under Closed Loop Control
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper presents a method of dynamic response analysis of a linear pulse motor under closed loop control, in which characteristics of the magnetic circuit and the control circuit of the motor are taken into consideration. This method was applied to a double-sided linear pulse motor with permanent magnets, and the influence of current control on the accelerating performance was investigated. The validity of the results was verified through comparison of computed and measured results. In addition, the optimum conditions for control were obtained from the results for the average dynamic thrust in each control mode.

articleTitle: Superconductivity in Nd2-xCexCuO4-∂ System
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of Ce doping and reduction on the superconductivity and electronic state of Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-x</inf>Ce<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>CuO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4-∂</inf> were investigated through measurements of the magnetization and X-ray absorption near-edge structure of the Cu-K edge of specimens annealed at various oxygen pressures and temperatures. The superconduction onset temperature and diamagnetism reach a peak at a Ce content of x=0.15. We found that the d electron density as estimated from the edge shift of the Cu-K edge absorption also has a peak around x=0.15. In addition, the d electron density increases with increasing reduction of the sample, and the magnitude of the superconduction diamagnetism becomes constant above a certain level of reduction. It is concluded that a d electron density above a certain critical value is necessary for the occurrence of superconduction in this system.

articleTitle: Superconducting Properties of Li-Doped Bi2Sr2CaCu2Ox Thick and Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of Li additon on the superconducting properties of Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CaCu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> thick and thin films was investigated. Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CaCu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> superconducting films were successfully obtained at low temperatures below 840°C by addition of Li2C03, which acted as a flux. The superconducting transition temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>) of films increases with increasing Li content, accompained by an increase in the c-axis lenghth. The thick and thin films had a T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">czero</inf> of 88K and 81K≫ respectively, higher than the values for undoped Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CaCu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>.

articleTitle: Continuous Fabrication and Perpendicular Recording Characteristics of Co-Cr Magnetic Tape
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new sputtering source (named an SPT target) was modified so as to enable high-rate deposition and continuous fabrication of Co-Cr composite perpendicular recording media. In order to improve the orientation and crystallinity of the Co-Cr layer and the permalloy backlayer, the aperture position was optimized and a magnetic return path plate was added to the target. The Co-Cr tape medium deposited on a 9 m thick polyimide film using this modified sputtering source showed good high-density recording performance.

articleTitle: An ac System Interruption Analysis of an Orthogonal-Core Type dc-ac Converter
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper describes an analysis of the transient response of an orthogonal core-type dc-ac converter for use in a photovoltaic power system. The analysis is based on a numerical model of an orthogonal core for use with the SPICE circuit analysis program. As one example of such a transient response analysis, we calculated the voltage and current of the dc-ac converter when its secondary is cut off from the ac system. The calculated results agreed well with measurements. The analytical method presented here is useful for predicting the behavior of a photovoltaic power system at the occurrence of ac system interruptions, line-to-line faults and various other faults.

articleTitle: Deposition Rate and Surface Smoothness of Fe3O4 Films Prepared by Light-Enhanced Ferrite Plating
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Polycrystalline Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> films were deposited by ferrite plating, irradiating the substrate surface with a Xe-lamp (350 W) and using FeCl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and NaNO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> as the reaction and oxidizing solutions, respectively. When the concentration of FeCl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> was high, the film surface was rough, with particle of 0.2~0.4 μm in size. As the concentration of FeCl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> decreased the film surface smoothness improved, but the film deposition rate decreased. Addition of dextran ((C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub>, n= 1200~1800) to the reaction solution improved the film surface smoothness without significantly lowering the deposition rate.

articleTitle: Superconducting Properties of YBa2Cu3O7-x Films Prepared by ECR Plasma-Assisted Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Using ECR plasma-assisted ing,¬ YBa<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7-x</inf> films with c-axis orientation were grown epitaxially on (100) SrTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> substrates. YBa<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7-x</inf> films prepared by ECR plasma-assisted sputtering had a smaller lattice constant c and a higher Tc than films prepared by magnetron sputtering alone. Optical emisssion spectroscopy measurements were performed during deposition to investigate the relationship between the superconducting properties of films and the plasma species in the ECR plasma. The film superconducting properties were closely related to the activated particles of oxygen in the ECR plasma.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Fe-Co-(Zr, Ta) Films Fabricated in Ar+N2 Plasma
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The possibility of realizing soft magnetic properties in 40 wt% Co-Fe alloy films with large magnetostriction constants, prepared by sputtering in Ar+N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plasma, is examined. The value of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> along the hard-axis direction of magnetization was about 10 Oe on annealing at 500°C. The soft magnetic properties of these films are determined primarily by lattice strain rather than by a macroscopically induced uniaxial magnetic anisotropy K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf>. The calculated magnetic anisotropy energy U in individual grains, taking account of the magnetoelastic energy, drastically increases with slight increases in the lattice strain. Therefore, in order to obtain excellent soft magnetic properties, lattice strain relaxation to less than 0.1% is important.

articleTitle: Soft Magnetic Properties of FeSiN/Ceramics Multi-Layers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic and structural properties of multilayer FeSiN/ceramic films produced by dual-type sputtering were investigated. Laminating of FeSiN with ceramic layers enhanced not only the frequency response of the permeability μ, but also the value of μ. These soft magnetic properties of as-deposited films were found to be strongly related to the substrate temperature T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sub</sub>, but were independent of the kind of ceramic used. Multilayered FeSiN/AIN films deposited at T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sub</sub>=300°C exhibited a large μ (at 5 MHz) of about 5,000 and a saturation induction B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> of more than 17 kG. SEM observation suggested that the soft magnetic properties of FeSiN-base multilayers arise from the decrease in magnetic anisotropy of the assembly of magnetically interacting small grains, and also from the (111) plane orientation of the grains. Most multilayered films exhibited greater thermal resistance to aging up to 600°C, because the ceramic layers prevent the growth of α-Fe grains.

articleTitle: Soft Magnetic Characteristics of Multilayered Films with Fe-Al-Si Layers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic properties of Fe-Al-Si/Fe, Fe-Al-Si/Fe-Si and Fe-Al-Si/Ni-Fe multilayer films prepared using rf sputtering equipment were investigated. These multilayer films had an initial permeability of more than 1000 prior to annealing; the Fe-Al-Si/Fe and Fe-Al-Si/Fe-Si multilayer films in particular had a high saturation flux density B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> of more than 14 kG. The magnetic properties of Fe-Al-Si/Ni-Fe multilayer film were nearly constant and independent of the layer thicknesses. In contrast, the thinner the layers of the Fe-Al-Si/Fe and Fe-Al-Si/Fe-Si multilayer films, the lower was the coercivity. In the latter films, the layer thickness dependence of the coercivity seems to be affected by lattice distortion and the crystal structure rather than by the size of crystallites.

articleTitle: Effects of Structure of FexN Intermediate Layers on Magnetic Properties of Fe/FexN Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: stract-Fe multilayered films with Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>N intermediate layers of various structures (Fe+Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>N, +Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>N, ϵ and Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>N) were prepared by reactive sputtering under various nitrogen partial pressure conditions. The effects of the Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>N intermediate layers on the coercivity (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>), saturation magnetization (B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>), and, structure of the Fe/Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>N multilayered films were investigated. Fe/Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>N multilayered films with intermediate layers prepared under conditions in which a single-layer Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>N film is obtained have a low H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> of less than 1 Oe. We found that the columnar growth of the Fe layers is interrupted in these films, grain sizes were reduced to less than 100 Å, and the lattice spacing of the -Fe (110) planes was increased. The low H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> of Fe/Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>N multilayered films is attributed to these factors.

articleTitle: Temperature Dependence of Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy in Fe/Pt Compositionally Modulated Multilayer Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The temperature dependences of the magnetization and magnetic anisotropy of Fe/Pt compositionally modulated multilayer films (CMFs) prepared by rf sputtering were investigated. The magnitude of the surface magnetic anisotropy K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> of Fe/Pt CMFs is nearly equal to that of Co/Pt CMFs at 77K and at room temperature. The absolute value of the volume magnetic anisotropy K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</sub> of Fe/Pt CMFs is about twice as large as that of Co/Pt CMFs. The K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> obtained from CMFs with thick Fe layers seems to remain nearly constant as the temperature is varied. However, K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</sub> decreases gradually with increasing temperature in the case of Fe/Pt CMFs. The relation between the saturation magnetization M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> (T) and the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sub> (T) are discussed.

articleTitle: Exchange Interactions in Metallic Superlattices
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In recent years transition metal superlattices such as Fe/Cr and Co/Cu have been found to exhibit interesting behavior such as a giant magnetoresistance and oscillating interlayer exchange interactions. This phenomena cannot be understood in terms of conventional theory of magnetic materials. We review recent experimental and theoretical work on exchange interactions, as well as the magnetic moment distribution in superlattices.

articleTitle: Estimation of Residual Magnetization by BEM
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A method for estimating the residual magnetization in a magnetic substance is proposed. This method is based on inverse analysis using the three-dimensional boundary element method. The distribution of the residual magnetization is calculated on the basis of the measured flux density near the surface. In this paper, singularities in the system equations for a simple problem are examined. This method is applied to a model of a permanent magnet; the results indicate that our method is useful for the estimation of residual magnetization.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Distribution of Shadow Mask having a Magnetic Circuit around a Frame Periphery and its Affection to the Electron Beam Trajectory
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The shadow mask in a color CRT is a soft thin iron plate which regulates the electron beam path. The mask may be magnetized by ambient magnetic fields, and the magnetization may change the beam path. As a result of the mask magnetization, the CRT screen may show color changes. We introduced magnetic circuits on the periphery of a shadow mask frame in order to decrease the mask and frame magnetization. The magnetic field distribution around the shadow mask was measured, and the effect of the circuits was evaluated through calculations of the change in electron trajectory. The addition of a magnetic circuit may be effective for decreasing the color change in CRT screens.

articleTitle: Relationship of Exciting Current to Noise-after-Write of Thin Film Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The behavior of noise-after-write in thin film heads was studied. The probability of noise-after-write events was decreased by applying a constant amplitude current or a decay amplitude current to the head coil, after shutting off the recording current. A constant-amplitude current was more effective for decreasing noise-after-write than a decay amplitude current. Comparison of the noise pulse of an Ni-Fe head and of a Co-Ta-Zr amorphous head showed that the former had a wider pulse width than the latter.

articleTitle: Wall Pinning Effect of Co-Zr-Nb Main-Pole Film on Recording Characteristics of Single-Pole Heads
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effect of the domain structure in main-pole film on the reproducing sensitivity was investigated for various single-pole type perpendicular magnetic heads. The reproducing sensitivity of heads made of a Co-Zr-Nb single-layer film becomes unstable and decreases with increasing closure domain size when the track width narrows and the anisotropy field H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> decreases. On the other hand, when the walls of closure domains are pinned by inserting small notches at both edges of a main-pole film, the magnetization rotates without any disturbance of the main domains. Using this novel method for controlling the domain structure, closure domains can be made smaller even for small H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>, and a stable and highly sensitive single-pole head can be obtained.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Recording Characteristics of CoPtB-O Perpendicular Recording Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: CoPtB-O films show a large perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and coercivity with a high saturation magnetization. For these reasons, they are promising high-density, high-output media. The recording characteristics of CoPtB-O perpendicular recording media were investigated. CoPtB-O films were prepared by rf sputtering on glass substrate for use as hard disk media, and their recording characteristics were measured using a MIG type ring head for VCRs with a spring suspension. A large reproduced output was obtained at 7.87 Mfc/m (200 kFCI) using a head with an appropriate gap length of 0.35 m. To obtain a large reproduced output at a high recording density, a medium must be used with a high perpendicular coercivity and a large perpendicular anisotropy, and a head gap length must be chosen which is appropriate to the recording wavelength.

articleTitle: An Influence of Head Field on the Transition Noise of Thin Film Disk
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The dependence of a field gradient on media noise was demonstrated. Medium noise was degraded under the influence of a secondary field with low field gradient. This influence was confirmed by the investigation of changes in media noise, which are based on the intrinsic micromagnetic media properties, for different field gradients. Reverse dc modulation noise and transition noise of low-H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> and high-H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> disks were evaluated using a single-sided MIG and a ferrite mini-monolithic head. Reverse dc modulation noise showed different values for the two heads, despite the fact that the medium was the same. The ratio of increase of reverse dc demagnetization noise to dc saturation noise, i.e. the reverse dc modulation ratio, was higher when the medium was evaluated using the MIG head, which can generate sharper field gradients in each medium. However, transition noise was lower when using the MIG head than when using the ferrite head. As a result, both the reverse dc modulation increase ratio and the transition noise level, which has been regarded as an intrinsic property of the medium, were strongly correlated to the field gradient.

articleTitle: A Study on Suitable Shapes of the Cloth Transformers for Reducing Power Loss
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper describes suitable shapes for cloth transformers with reduced power loss. The self-inductance, leakage reactance and resistance (equivalent to the iron loss) were measured for various core arrangement patterns to evaluate the characteristics of such cloth transformers. A cloth transformer shape which proved to be optimal for reducing power losses was found.

articleTitle: Some Considerations on Design of the Transcutaneous Transformer
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: We utilized two spiral coils with amorphous magnetic fibers for transcutaneous power transmission to an implantable artificial heart which is electrically actuated. Rises in temperature occurring during power transmission constitutes a serious obstacle to practical application. The operation of the transmitting coils is analyzed using an equivalent circuit, and the quantity of magnetic flux flowing in the amorphous fibers is discussed. The results were employed in the design of thinner transmitting coils.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Characteristics in the Quadri-Layered M-O Film with Overwritability
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors investigated the external magnetic field characteristics of exchange-coupled quadrilayer magnetooptic film in direct overwriting by optical modulation. The external field dependence of the recording characteristics was studied through the temperature dependence of the reversal field and the mechanism of direct overwriting. In direct overwriting by optical modulation, an upper limit to the external field exists due to the "low" process. Here the process of initialization of the writing layer, unique to the quadrilayer film, did not affect the lower limit of the external field. A wide external field margin was obtained under conditions of practical use, and effective fluctuations in the external field did not affect the recording laser power margin.

articleTitle: Substrate Bias Effect on Magnetic Properties of Sputter Deposited Co/Pt Multilayers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Co/Pt multilayer films were prepared by rf sputtering with a negative substrate bias voltage (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>) applied. The morphology of the multilayer films changed from a columnar structure to a fine-textured structure on applying the bias V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>. A bias voltage of about -30 V improves the flatness and sharpness of the interface and causes a decrease in the perpendicular coercivity, because of the reduction of pinning effects at the layer surfaces and/or column boundaries. In low-coercivity films prepared with a bias voltage applied, Bitter observations clearly revealed stripe domains.

articleTitle: Spinal Reflex Evoked by Magnetic Stimulation
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A noninvasive method of selective magnetic stimulation of the spinal roots is proposed. The basic idea is to concentrate induced eddy currents in a target region using a pair of opposing pulsed magnetic fields. A figure-eight coil is positioned outside the median of the back so that time-varying magnetic fields pass through the body in opposite directions around the target area. The spinal roots of human subjects and animals were stimulated magnetically. Each spine level was stimulated selectively, producing electromyographic (EMG) waves related to both the H-reflex and the M-waves. Experimental results indicate that the M-wave can be produced by currents flowing either in the rostral or caudal direction, whereas the H-reflex is generated by currents flowing in the caudal direction. The H-reflex elicited by magnetic stimulation will be useful for diagnosis of diseases of the neuro-muscular system.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Magnetoresistance of Multilayers with Two Different Magnetic Layers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The spin-dependent electron scattering in multilayer films consisting of Cu and two magnetic materials, Co and Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf> alloy, was investigated. In the magnetization process, a giant ferrimagnetic state is realized at moderate external field because of the difference in coercive forces. When the magnetizations of two ferromagnetic layers are antiparallel to each other, the electrical resistivity increases due to spin-dependent electron scattering. The MR ratio was observed to be 10% at room temperature and 28% at 80K in the multilayers film [Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf> (25Å) /Cu (55Å)/Co (25å)/Cu (55Å)]×l5 film.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties and Structure of FeN/AlN Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic properties and structure of FeN/AlN multilayered films deposited by r.f. magnetron sputtering were studied. H<sub>c</sub> decreased as the ratio of FeN to AlN layer thickness became small. H<sub>c</sub> also decreased with decreasing film thickness of FeN/AlN bilayers. H<sub</sub> and 4πM<sub>s</sub> in a 22Å/11Å multilayered film were 1 Oe and 8.5 kG, respectively. The film had high permeability, μ', 800 at 5 MHz and 650 even at 100 MHz because of high resistivity. SEM observation and μ-AES analysis revealed the film had a layered structure. X-ray diffraction made it clear that high permeability was ascribed to fine grains and smaller lattice mismatch between layers compared to thick layered films.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Anisotropic Pr-Fe-B Melt-Spun Ribbons
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic properties and microstructure of Pr-Fe-B(Ga) melt-spun ribbons prepared by the single- or twin-roller method were studied. A texture with the c-axis normal to the surface was observed in slowly quenched ribbons, and showed a strong dependence on composition. Addition of Ga is effective for increasing the coercivity and the c-axis alignment of ribbons. Magnetic measurements of powders obtained by crushing ribbon samples prepared by the twin-roller method revealed that the powders solidified in a paraffin bath with a magnetic field of 12 kOe applied had a high coercivity of iH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>=13.8 kOe and a higher remanence than did powders solidified without a field applied. Observations of the microstructure of cast alloys suggest that the strong c-axis alignment arises from the rapid quenching.

articleTitle: Soft Magnetic Properties of Sputtered FeZrBM (M=Co,Ni,Cr,V) Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The soft magnetic properties of sputtered FeZrB films with Co, Ni, Cr or V added were investigated. While FeZrB ternary films did not exhibit soft magnetic properties in these experiments, addition of a few percent of a fourth element raises the permeability sufficiently for magnetic head applications. These changes correspond to the variations in the film magnetostriction. Any of the above additives changes the magnetostriction constant of FeZrB film from negative to positive. However, the effects of Co or Ni addition on crystallization are different from those of Cr or V. On adding Co or Ni, the crystallization temperature T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> is lowered, the lattice spacing L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> increases and the saturation magnetic flux density B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> rises, while addition of Cr or V makes T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> higher, L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> smaller and B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> lower. With respect to producing soft magnetic properties, Co is the best of the four added elements, and Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">87.6</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.2</inf>Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5.8</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.3</inf> exhibits excellent soft magnetic properties after annealing at 550C (B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> approximately 18 kG, approximately 5000).

articleTitle: Crystallographic Structures, Magnetic Properties and Their Change Due to Annealing in Co/Cr Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The crystallographic structure and magnetic properties of Co/Cr multilayer films were investigated. Films are comprised of hcp Co and bcc Cr. The crystallographic structure of the film was affected by the substrate temperature, particularly in the case of small layer thicknesses. Films sputtered at high substrate temperatures had larger perpendicular anisotropy than those sputtered at low temperatures. The saturation magnetization per unit Co volume decreases with decreasing Co layer thickness. Alloying at interfaces causes the decrease of Co layer magnetization. The thickness of the alloy layers is estimated at 2.5 Å to 5.0 Å. Films prepared on glass substrates were annealed in vacuum at 300°C and 500°C. Diffusion coefficients and activation energies were calculated from the decrease in magnetization due to annealing; the activation energy for diffusion was between 0.2 and 0.5 eV.

articleTitle: Thermal Stability of Soft Magnetic Properties in Fe/CoZr Multilayer Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The thermal stability of the structural and soft magnetic properties of sputter-deposited Fe/Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">92</inf>Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> multilayer films was investigated. The thermal stability of the film coercivity is improved by using very thin bilayers. The good thermal stability is attributed to the suppression of grain growth in the film plane. When the Fe layers are made thinner than 10 nm, a low coercivity of less than 2 Oe can be obtained even after annealing at 600°C, and an effective permeability of about 2000 can be obtained after annealing at 500°C.

articleTitle: Development of Permeability Measuring Instrument
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Recent electronic devices often use nonmagnetic components with very small permeabilities of less than 1.010. It is difficult to measure the permeability of such materials using the usual techniques. In order to enable measurement in such cases, an improved instrument for permeability measurement was devised. In this instrument, which is based on a type of differential transformer, the material is magnetized by an exciting coil and the resulting magnetic response is detected. The response consists of two components, one from the magnetization and one from eddy currents. The distribution of the magnetization and the eddy currents within the material were estimated using the finite element method applied to analysis of electromagnetic fields. On the basis of this analysis, an improved instrument was developed which is capable of measuring permeabilities of less than 1.010 even in small-size components.

articleTitle: Dependence of Magnetoresistance and Magnetic Properties on the Deposition Conditions and Temperature in Ni-Co-Fe Alloy Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetoresistance effect and magnetic properties of Ni-Co-Fe thin films prepared under various deposition conditions were studied. An anisotropic magnetoresistivity ratio of above 5% was obtained. The value of ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">av</sub> depends on the substrate temperature and film thickness, but Δρ does not. Both ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">av</sub> and Δρ were measured as functions of temperature; the results showed that the temperature dependence of ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">av</sub> is quite similar to that of the MR ratio.

articleTitle: Non-Destructive Testing with Magnetic Sensor Using Rotational Magnetic Flux
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper presents a new nondestructive testing (NDT) method which utilizes rotational magnetic flux. In conventional eddy current NDT, the magnetic sensor is driven by an ac or dc current. Consequently, the magnetic field generated in the magnetic material is aligned in a single direction. However, in order to estimate the shape or position of an unknown defect, a two-dimensional alternating magnetic flux density vector is necessary. An NDT system utilizing rotational magnetic flux is proposed. In this system, the magnitude and phase value are measured and used to obtain information about the defect.

articleTitle: Effects of Bias Modulation on Magnetic Properties of Co/Pt Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Co/Pt multilayer films were prepared by rf sputtering. A substrate bias voltage V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> of 0 V to -70 V was applied while sputtering either Co or Pt onto glass substrate. In Co biased films (prepared with V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> applied while depositing Co only), the perpendicular anisotropy K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> increases with V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> and peaks at -50 V, because the flatness and sharpness of the interfaces and the fcc (111) orientation are optimum at this bias voltage. The increase in K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> arises from the improvement in both the surface and volume anisotropy. On the other hand, in Pt biased films mixing of Co and Pt occurs at layer boundaries, resulting in a decrease in K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</sub> for V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>≥-50 V.

articleTitle: Hysteresis Reduction Effect of the Cross-Shaking Technique Applied to Magnetostrictive Torque Sensors
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new method for reducing hysteresis is proposed for magnetic head type torque sensors based on the magnetostrictive effect. This method adopts magnetic shaking, in which the shaking field is applied perpendicularly to the exciting field. The hysteresis and sensitivity of a quench-hardened steel shaft (SCM415) 25 mm in diameter subjected to torques ranging from -490 N-m to 490 N-m were measured. The hysteresis was reduced by a factor of 10 and the sensitivity was increased by a factor of 2 for an exciting frequency of 10 kHz and shaking frequency of 1 kHz. The relationship of the shaking frequency and the shaking effect to the total power consumption is also discussed.

articleTitle: Observation of Flux Density Distribution in YBa2Cu3Ox Superconductor Thin Film Using Bi-Substituted Iron Garnet Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Bi-substituted iron garnet film with a large Faraday rotation and perpendicular magnetization was prepared, and the film domain patterns were used to observe the flux penetrating superconducting YBa<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> thin films. Observations were performed for both square and disk-shaped YBa<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> films. The penetration behavior depends on defects and the shape of the film. We confirmed that the flux density in superconducting film as observed through the iron garnet film domain patterns was nearly the same as that estimated from the sample magnetization.

articleTitle: In-Situ Observation of Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect and Resistance of Fe Island Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetooptic Kerr effect and electric resistance of Fe deposited on fused quartz substrates were observed during ultra-high vacuum deposition. Resistance measurements show that Fe forms islands on the quartz substrates, and that films with such an island morphology turn into continuous films at about 115 Å thickness at room temperature. The magnetooptic Kerr effect is observable from a thickness of 16 Å, and a remanence magnetization appears from 21 Å.

articleTitle: Some Considerations on the Design Method of Parametric Motor Utilizing the Equivalent Circuit
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Parametric motors have many excellent features compared with ordinary single-phase motors, and are expected to find many practical applications. In this paper, methods for improving the characteristics of parametric motors in order to render them more practically useful are discussed, utilizing the equivalent circuit of an induction motor. Implementation of such methods results in a parametric motor having excellent performance. Improved power factor, output power, and efficiency are achieved both by increasing the effective magnetic flux through an enlarged rotor diameter and by determining the optimum rotor length. The motor size and weight were reduced by decreasing the dimensions of the magnetic flux path of the exciting core without impairing the motor characteristics.

articleTitle: Soft Magnetic Properties for Fe-B Films Sputtered in Ar+N2 Plasma
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe-B films sputtered in Ar+N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> plasma were investigated in order to obtain film with high initial permeability. Importance was placed on elucidation of the relation between the initial permeability μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub> and parameters of the film structure such as the phase, grain size, and lattice strain. Fe-B (1 to 4 at% B) films sputtered in Ar+5%N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> plas-ma exhibit a high μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub> of about 2000 after annealing at 400 °C, and about 1000 after annealing at 500 °C. The results of X-ray and electron diffraction patterns indicate that films with high μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub> consist of the α phase. By comparing this with results for Fe-N films, it is suggested that the high μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub> of Fe-B-N films is caused by the reduction of grain sizes and induced lattice strain, as well as other metallurgical structures such as in homogeneities.

articleTitle: The Effect of Addition of Rare Earth Elements on Magnetostriction in bec Fe-Co Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetostriction and magnetic properties of bcc Fe-Co-Sm alloys produced by dc triode sputtering have been investigated. Addition of 3 at% Sm suppressed the large positive magnetostriction of bec Fe-Co alloys, resulting in almost zero magnetostriction for bcc Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</inf> alloys. These nonmagnetostrictive alloys show a high saturation magnetization of about 210 emu/g, and thus are thought to be useful as soft magnetic materials.

articleTitle: Development of 2" Diameter Co-Cr Video Floppy Disk
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Four technical problems have delayed the commercialization of Co-Cr video floppy disks (VFDs): (1) smooth head contact, (2) durability and reliability in various environments, (3) significant improvement of recording performance, and (4) attainment of reasonable cost. This paper demonstrates the feasibility of simultaneously achieving (1) and (3). As for (2), durability has been achieved at 23°C, 50% RH and at 40°C, 80% RH. Video image quality comparable to MP-VFD playback can be obtained at 1/6 the track width, namely 10 μm.

articleTitle: Fe and FeCo Thin Films Prepared by Ar+N2 Ion-Beam Sputtering
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The characteristics of ferromagnetic metal nitride thin films as potential magnetooptic recording media fabricated by ion-beam sputtering were studied, with special emphasis on factors relating to the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy. The transmittance of films was found to be related to the c-axis orientation of the Fe and FeCo nitride. The FeCo nitride thin films had a large Faraday rotation of θ=7.7 deg/μm at 780 nm. Fe and FeCo nitride thin films were found to have a high corrosion resistance in NaCl water solution. TEM observations of cross-sections of ferromagnetic metal nitride thin films revealed a columnar microstructure composed of an amorphous phase and a crystalline phase, with grains of 10 nm or less in diameter.

articleTitle: Preparation of Co-Cr-Ta Hard Disk High Density Recording Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In order to improve the anisotropy field distribution of Co-Cr recording media, the effect of Ta addition was investigated. It was found that by adding Ta the initial Co-Cr layer with poor crystal orientation is eliminated, and crystal orientation and crystallinity are drastically improved. It was also confirmed that the anisotropy field distribution of the Co-Cr-Ta layer is narrowed to one-third that of the Co-Cr layer. To clarify the effect of Ta addition on recording characteristics, Co-Cr-Ta/Nb-permalloy double-layer media were prepared and their recording characteristics were measured. The Co-Cr-Ta media showed a sharp magnetization distribution and higher reproduced voltage at high densities than did the Co-Cr media.

articleTitle: Soft Magnetic Properties of Fe-Si-N Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The crystal structure and magnetic properties of sputter-deposited Fe-Si-N films were investigated. Fe-Si-N films had a single α-Fe phase, and with higher N content, two phases, α-Fe and γ'-Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>N. A coercivity H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> lower than 1 Oe was obtained for single α-Fe phase films. The permeability μ was found to be strongly related to the substrate temperature T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sub</sub> during deposition. For example, deposition at T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sub</sub>=230°C gave rise to μ=3600 at 10 MHz. Such high values were obtained in single α-Fe phase films, which consisted of fine crystal grains with a (111) plane orientation. The permeability of films with a high Si concentration was found to have high thermal stability.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Te-Doped Bi-Pb-Sr-Ca-Cu Superconductors
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic properties of Te-doped Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.4</inf>Pb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</inf>Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Ca<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Te<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf> superconductors were studied. Samples with x= 0.05 to 0.2, fired at 850°C for 50 hours in air, showed zero resistance above 100K. The volume fraction of the superconducting phases was increased by Te doping, and was maximum at x=0.1. On measuring hysteresis loops at 77K, the residual magnetization for the sample with x= 0.1 was found to be much larger than that for x=0. The critical current density for Te-doped samples was improved under high magnetic fields. These results suggest that Te doping is effective for increasing the pinning force. WDX analysis indicated that high-Tc phases contained 0.6 at% Te.

articleTitle: Properties of Fe-Zr-N Thin Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Gases emerging from Fe-Zr-N films with various compositions during heating were analyzed by thermal desorption spectroscopy. The structures and magnetic properties of films were also investigated. H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and Ar were detected at 300-400°C, 500°C and 650°C, respectively. Larger amounts of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> were emitted by films which contained larger amounts of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The changes in composition of films due to the emerging N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is as follows. The composition changed for N/Zr ratios ranging from N/Zr≫1 to N/Zr~1, but was unchanged when N/Zr1. A (100) preferred orientation occurred in films in which the composition was N~Zr≫8 at% in the as-deposited state, while either a (100) orientation or random orientation occurred in all other cases. Under the former conditions, Fe-Zr-N films showed excellent soft magnetic properties and thermal stability up to 700°C.

articleTitle: On the Characteristics of a Phase Converter
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A phase converter driven by a stable phase sequence has been developed and studied experimentally to determine its voltage regulation characteristics. This converter consists of two parts: a three-phase ferroresonant constant voltage stabilizer, and a phase shifter circuit, which serves to generate a pseudo three-phase voltage supply and to fix the phase sequence of the stabilizer. In order to achieve stable operation and satisfactory performance, the stabilizer was improved by the use of a harmonic filter tuned to the 2.5th harmonic, and the phase-shifter circuit is driven by a balanced phase condition of the circuit. New criteria for evaluating voltage regulation are introduced, and the performance of the equipment is discussed on the basis of experimental data, with reference to three reduced circuit parameters--α and ß, concerned with the phase shifter circuit, and for the stabilizer.

articleTitle: Soft Magnetic Properties of Fe/Fe-Hf-C Multilayered Films with High Thermal Stability
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic and structural properties of rf sputter-deposited Fe/Fe-Hf-C multilayer films were investigated. Columnar growth of Fe was interrupted only when as-deposited Fe-Hf-C layers were amorphous. The Fe-Hf-C layers crystallize by annealing into α-Fe and HfC with small grains of size several nanometers. These multilayer films exhibited good soft magnetic properties (coercivity 26 A/m and permeability 3700) due to the small Fe grain sizes of each layer, as well as a high saturation flux density (approx. 2.0 T). Interdiffusion between layers during high-temperature annealing was suppressed by the formation of a strong bond between Hf and C in the Fe-Hf-C layers. Furthermore, fine HfC particles inhibited the growth of Fe grains. Thus a high permeability of more than 1000 was maintained even after annealing at 1023 K. In addition, near-zero-magnetostriction films were obtained by addition of a small amount of Co to the Fe-Hf-C larers, without any resulting decrease in permeability.

articleTitle: Thermal Stability of Fe-Zr/Fe-Zr-N Soft Magnetic Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: stract-Fe-Zr/Fe-Zr-N multilayered films were prepared by alternation of Fe-Zr sputtering and electron cyclotron resonance (ECR) plasma nitridation. Thermal stability of the films' soft magnetic properties was investigated. A saturation flux density of B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>=1.8 T, coercivity H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>=88 A/m and relative permeability μ'≫3000 (at 20 MHz) were obtained for Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">92</sub>Zr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sub>/Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">92</sub>Zr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sub>-N multilayered film after annealing at 773K for 3600 s. Addition of Zr to Fe/Fe-N multilayered films effectively improves the thermal stability of soft magnetic properties.

articleTitle: In-Plane Anisotropy and Recording Characteristics of Vacuum Deposited Co-Cr Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In fabricating Co-Cr films using a continuous vacuum deposition system, the angle at which the vapor beam is incident on the substrate affects the magnetic properties and recording characteristics of the resulting film. Co-Cr films deposited at incident angles from 55° to 20° and from 70° to 20° are anisotropic, while films deposited at incident angles from 20° to -20° are isotropic in the film plane. The azimuth angle dependence of the reproduced output in these films correlates fairly well with the angular dependence of M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> in the film plane. The isolated playback wave-form from films deposited with the angle of incidence ranging from 55° to 20° has a MMF dependence in the normal head scanning direction, whereas that of films deposited from 70° to 20° is independent of the MMF in both the normal and the reverse head scanning directions.

articleTitle: An Analysis of the Behavior of Orthogonal-Core Type Push-Pull Parametric Transformer with Iron and Copper Losses
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper describes an analysis of the behavior of orthogonal-core type push-pull parametric transformers, taking the iron loss of the orthogonal-cores and the copper loss of the windings into consideration. The analysis was performed for the magnetic circuit of the orthogonal-core under magnetic saturation and with hysteresis. To improve the accuracy of calculations, the saturation characteristic was approximated by a series which includes terms of up to 21st order in the flux, and the hysteresis curve by a series including terms of up to 5th order in the exciting voltage. The calculated results show good agreement with experimental data. The analytical method presented here is useful for optimizing the design of push-pull parametric transformers.

articleTitle: Recent Technical Development in MRI
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Medical MR imaging techniques have come into wide use in routine clinical examinations. In addition to the anatomical and structural information obtained for use in clinical diagnoses, other new information, such as functional and dynamical data, is also becoming available. New features are being added by the technique called as fast- and ultra-fast imaging, MR angiography and 3D-volume imaging. For the development of such new techniques, precise control of the magnetic field gradient and rf pulses are required. The flexibility and variability of NMR pulse sequences are utilized to improve the MR imaging method and extend it into new fields of application.

articleTitle: High Frequency Response of Magnetization of Thin-Film Heads
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetization response of thin film heads in the high frequency region was studied using a scanning Kerr effect microscope. The area of large magnetization rotation converges gradually to the central region of the core of a thin film head as the frequency is increased. Above 20 MHz, the domain structure changes, i.e. the number of domains increases with increasing frequency and there is less curvature at both sides of the 180° walls. As a result, the region of convergence of the magnetization rotation broadens. Comparing the static magnetization direction and the magnetization response, it was found that at high frequencies the magnetization in the track direction goes through large rotations, while that inclined from the track direction undergoes only small rotations.

articleTitle: Contrast Reversal of Magneto-Optical Domain Image by Photo-Elastic Modulator
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Two methods were employed to study the fast contrast reversal of magnetic domain images by a photoelastic modulator (PEM). A PEM combined with a quarter-wave plate acts as a polarization rotator, and enables domain observation with fast contrast reversal under exposure to pulsating light. Contrast reversal in as little as 10 μs is possible. However, the PEM is driven sinusoidally, hence the domain contrast is modulated, resulting in a low average contrast. When a PEM was employed as a phase compensator with a garnet film polarization rotator, it could dynamically compensate for unwanted contributions from the ellipticity of the sample and the garnet rotator. This combination provided not only fast contrast reversal, but even higher contrast compared with that obtained in conventional methods involving the mechanical rotation of an analyzer. In the latter method, a domain image contrast of 0.82 was derived theoretically, and a contrast of 0.76 was obtained experimentally, for domains with θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub>=0.19° and χ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub>=0.13°, whereas the contrast using the conventional mechanical method was 0.72.

articleTitle: Texturing of Glass Disks by Microgrid Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new texturing method for glass disk substrates is proposed. Thin perforated plastic film (microgrid) is first formed on a substrate, and then the substrate is chemically etched using the perforated Aim as a mask. The textured substrate has micron-size round holes distributed uniformly on the surface. A 0.2 μm thick magnetic film and 0.025 μm thick carbon overcoat were sputter-deposited on the textured substrate and CSS tests were carried out using an Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-TiC minislider head. The microgrid-textured disk of 3 μm hole diameter and of 0.1 μm hole depth showed a good friction coefficient as low as 0.4 after 25600 CSS cycles. This result is better than that of a mechanically textured disk of similar surface roughness.

articleTitle: MR and Hall Effect in Ni-Fe, Ni-Co Films at Low Temperature
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The anisotropic magnetoresistance (Δρ, ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and Δρ/ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>), the ordinary Hall co-efficient (R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>), the extraordinary Hall coefficient (R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>), and the saturation magnetization (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>) were measured for Ni-Co, Ni-Fe and Ni-Cu binary alloy thin films in the range from 77K to 300K. As a result, the increase of Δρ and Δρ/ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> corresponds well to the minimum R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> ranged from -1.0 to -2.0×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup> V-cm/A-Oe and to near-zero R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>.
