The increase in Δρ/ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> corresponds well to the decrement in absolute value of the coefficient C. The maximum of Δρ/ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> was found to be obtained around the zero value of C.

articleTitle: Thin Film Opto-Electric Transformer
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A thin film optoelectric transformer consisting of a p-n junction photocell (500×500 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and a multilayer spiral coil transformer (1.4×1.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), monolithically fabricated on a Si substrate, is proposed, and its fundamental characteristics are described. The optical power from a layer diode (LD) is converted into electric power by the photocell, and the photocurrent is then converted into an output voltage V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> by the miniaturized transformer. In these experiments, both the primary and the secondary coils had double layers of rectangular spiral coils and had tire same number of turns, i.e. the device was a 1:1 transformer. The frequency dependence of the inductance L of the double-layer coil with an outer core was measured. Annealed magnetic film had better characteristics for inductance than did unannealed film. Circuit simulations were performed by a PSpice simulator using experimental values for parameters; the experimental results could be explained satisfactorily by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Development of Artificial Heart and Intra Aortic Balloon Pump Using Linear Pulse Motor
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper deals with an Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump (IABP) and Artificial Heart (AH) using linear pulse motors (LPMs). The device characteristics may be summarized as follows. The maximum static thrusts of the LPM for the IABP and the LPM for the AH were 530 N and 107 N respectively. The kinetic thrusts of the LPMs for the IABP and for the AH were 350 N and 67 N respectively. The target thrust values were obtained in experiments. In mock tests, the expansion time of the balloon in the LPM-driven IABP was found to be 100 ms. In future, existing IABPs will be miniaturized by the adoption of LPMs. The instantaneous flow rate of the LPM-driven AH can be controlled by employing an acceleration drive pattern with the LPM. In mock circulatory tests, an LPM-driven AH delivered a flow rate of 5.3 L/min at a pulse rate of 100 beats/min, sufficient to sustain an adult's life. The temperature of the AH rose 11C during operation; suppression of increases in temperature is recognized as an important problem.

articleTitle: Substitution Effect of Fe Sites in Nd2Fe14B
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: In order to investigate the magnetic contributions of each iron site of Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf>B, the magnetic properties of Nd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf>B (M=Al, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, Ga, Pt) were measured, and the preferential occupation of Fe sites by M atoms was studied by Mossbauer spectroscopy. The Mossbauer spectra were analyzed by a method of our own devising, which takes into account the effect of the environment and the degree of preference of each Fe site. These analyses revealed that the Curie temperature T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> increases with increases in the lattice parameter c accompanying preferential substitution of M atoms at the k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and j<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> sites, but decreases when j<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> site is preferentially occupied by M atoms. It seems that the ferromagnetic interaction between Fe planes increases with the lattice expansion and decreases as j<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> site is occupied by M atoms. On the other hand, T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> decreases when there is preferential substitution at c site. This fact suggests that T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> is related to the interaction between Fe and Nd atoms.

articleTitle: Maskless Patterning of Fe3O4 Films by Laser-Enhanced Ferrite Plating
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: By irradiating glass substrate with an Ar laser (=514.5 nm) beam, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> film was deposited in an aqueous solution at rates as high as 2.35 m/min. By synchronously moving the substrate during plating, we successfully drew patterns (letters in the Roman alphabet and dots) of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> film by selected-area growth, without the need for a mask. This technique is useful for fabricating fine-patterned film devices (e.g. microwave circulators and isolators), using as substrate such non-heat-resistant materials as GaAs ICs.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Magnetic Properties of Fe Thin Films on a Substrate Excited by SAW
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Fe films of thickness 300Å were prepared by electron beam evaporation and dc magnetron sputtering onto LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> single-crystal substrate excited by surface acoustic waves (SAWs) at 45 MHz. A biaxial anisotropy was induced in the film plane for evaporated films with the substrate excited at 8 V, but was not induced at all in sputtered films. The saturation magnetization M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> of the evaporated films increased with increasing excitation voltage, and reached the bulk value at an excitation voltage of 8 V. However, the M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> of sputtered films was not changed by SAW excitation. The density of evaporated films was close to the density of bulk Fe at an excitation voltage of 8 V. This fact shows that the structure of evaporated films changed from a porous to a dense structure with SAW excitation. Further, the film surface became smooth when the substrate was excited.

articleTitle: Reverse Domain Propagation in Fe-Co Base Amorphous Wires
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors estimated the damping constants of domain propagation due to eddy currents and spin relaxation in Fe-Si-B amorphous magnetostrictive wire. The damping constant in the outer shell of the wire was about 57% of the total damping constant. Domains at the wire surface before and after Large Barkhausen discontinuities were observed. It was concluded that this remarkably large damping in the outer shell is caused by a magnetic interaction between the core and the shell which takes place during propagation of a domain wall in the core.

articleTitle: Magnetic Properties of Tb/Fe Multilayers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Tb/Fe multilayer films with Fe/Tb layer thickness ratios of 1/1 and 1/2 were prepared on glass substrate by rf sputtering. The Fe layers were poly-crystalline when their thickness d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fe</inf> was greater than 17 Å. When d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fe</inf> was less than or near 17 Å, the Fe layer became amorphous. Films with d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Fe</inf>=17 Å exhibited small magnetizations and spin glass-like magnetization curves, because of the antiferromagnetic nature of amorphous Fe. Magnetic properties changed as a result of changes in the crystallographic structure.

articleTitle: Spin Flopping in Gd/Fe and Gd/Co Multilayers Prepared by an Evaporation with Oblique Incidences
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Gd/Fe and Gd/Co multilayer films, prepared by electron beam evaporation with oblique incidence, exhibit a uniaxial magnetic anisotropy in the film plane owing to anisotropic atomic coupling at the interfaces. When the bilayer thicknesses are between 16 and 22 Å for Gd/Fe and are 12 Å for Gd/Co, the M-H loop in an easy-axis direction at room temperature is rectangular under low fields, and an abrupt increase in magnetization, i.e. spin flopping, occurs at about 0.5 kOe in Gd/Fe multilayer film and near 1.0 kOe in Gd/Co multilayer film.

articleTitle: Shape Effect of Magnetoresistance Effect
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetoresistance of Ni-Co-Fe ternary alloy thin films, both circular and rectangular with varying widths, was studied. Sample resistivity was measured using a four-point probe. Using the method of images, the true value of ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">av</sub> can be obtained for each film, but that of Δρ cannot, because the angle between the current direction and the magnetization direction is not uniform within the film. The behavior of ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">av</sub> and Δρ can be explained exactly using the finite element method, enabling analysis of the magnetoresistance of films of various shapes.

articleTitle: Magnetostriction of (Fe-Co)3 Tb Compounds and Amorphous Fe3 Tb Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetostriction of (Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub> Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>) Tb (0≤×≤1.0) compounds and amorphous Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Tb alloys were measured at room temperature and at 77K. The value of λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">″</sub>-λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sub> at 77K and 20 kOe of (Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Tb compounds increases drastically from 1500×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> to 3000×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> as x is increased from 0 to 1.0. The value of λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">″</sub>-λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⊥</sub> for amorphous Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Tb is about 30 to 40% smaller than the value for the crystalline material. The effect of Co substitution on the magnetostriction of (Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>)Tb compounds is discussed on the basis of the single ion model. The magnetic field dependence of magnetostriction in Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>Tb amorphous alloy is also discussed in connection with the magnetization process.

articleTitle: Direct Observation of Magnetic Flux Behavior in High-Tc Oxide Superconductors
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic flux behavior in YBa<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> specimens under various applied fields was observed at 10K and 77K using the Faraday effect of an iron garnet film with stripe magnetic domains. The magnetic flux distribution was determined by optical observation of the domain structure in the iron garnet film placed on the sample. The magnetic flux gradients in a crystal fabricated by the Melt-Powder-Melt-Growth (MPMG) method and in a thin film were in good agreement with those predicted by the critical state model at both 10K and 77K. On the other hand, in a sintered sample the flux penetrated through the superconducting weak-link regions, and no flux gradient was observed at 77K.

articleTitle: Single Crystal Fe Films Prepared by a Low Kinetic Energy Sputtering Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The ga-flow-sputtring (GFS) method, in which atoms with very low kinetic energies (≪0.1 eV) are deposited, was studied as a means of growing single-crystal α-Fe films on MgO(001). These films were characterized by reflection high-energy electron diffraction, X-ray diffraction and Kerr-effect magnetometry. The results suggested that single-crystal Fe films grow at a substrate temperature of about 400°C and under a pressure of 1 Torr, at a growth rate of 1100 Å/min.

articleTitle: Structural and Magnetic Characteristics of Dy/Yb Superlattices
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Dy/Yb superlattices with atomicscale periodicity were fabricated by the molecular beam epitaxy method. Reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) and X-ray diffraction analyses revealed that the fcc Yb layers grew epitaxially on a cleaved NaCl substrate, while Dy layers were found to have the hep structure with a [102] and/or [110] orientation. Thermal hysteresis resulting from different cooling conditions was observed in Dy/Yb superlattices. The magnetic spins of zero-field-cooled superlattices reoriented from the magnetic-frozen states to ferromagnetic states when heated from 4.2K to a specified temperature and then cooled back to 4.2K under a magnetic field.

articleTitle: Tablet Using Matteucci Effect of Amorphous Magnetic Wires
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This article describes a new tablet for inputting handwritten characters to computers using amorphous magnetic wires employing the Matteucci effect, which is sensitive to perpendicular ac magnetic fields. The Matteucci voltage e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</inf> with a double-frequency-pulse shaped ac voltage is induced across the ends of an amorphous wire when an arbitrary point is vertically magnetized by a pen-shaped coil with an amorphous magnetic core. The value of e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</inf> was nearly constant as the pen was slid along the wire, but rapidly decreased with pen displacement vertical to the wire. An amorphous wire matrix was constructed, with each of the ten wires in the X and Y directions spaced at 5 mm intervals, and with Matteucci voltage pulses converted to dc voltages through peak-holders. Handwritten characters are displayed on a microcomputer display using a multiplexer, A/D converter, and position detection software.

articleTitle: Effect of Annealing on the Magnetic Properties of Co/Fe Multilayer Films Deposited with Different Background Pressures
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The effects of post-deposition annealing on the magnetic properties of Co/Fe multilayer films sputtered with different background pressures (P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>) were examined. Films were deposited by dc magnetron sputtering with a P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> of 1.0×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> or 9.0×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> Torr, and were annealed in vacuum at temperatures between 100°C and 600°C for one hour. The saturation magnetization of films increased on annealing at and above 300°C, indicating the alloying of Co and Fe. The coercivity (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>) of films deposited in a high P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> was 1 Oe before annealing, but increased on annealing at and above 300°C. The H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> of films deposited in a low P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> was 50 Oe before annealing, but decreased rapidly when annealed at and above 200°C, reaching a minimum of 8 Oe at 500°C. The differences in magnetic properties for differnet P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub> are mainly due to the different oxygen contents of the films.

articleTitle: A Production of the Magnetic Neuron Network
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: An artificial neural network circuit using a magnetic device has been developed. The network consists of magnetic neurons and magnetic synapses. A magnetic neuron starts oscillating when the sum if its input currents exceed the threshold level, and its frequency varies according to the input level. Magnetic synapses can be easily controlled through a bias current. The network fabricated in this work has a three-layer structure, with two input gates and a single output. By adjusting the synapses, 16 kinds of logic functions can be realized. It is, however, very difficult to set correctly all the weights of the synapses in a large-scale network, so we adopted a learning technique. Only the input sets and the ideal output are given; the weights are corrected according to a learning algorithm that eventually attains ideal operation. That is, the network learns.

articleTitle: Sensormagnetics
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: "Sensor magnetics" refers to a new field in applied magnetics involving sensors using magnetic materials and their applications in sensing technologies. Recently such magnetic sensors have come into wide use, not only in conventional industrial measurement, but also in the fields of mechatronics, electronics, medical electronics, and information technologies. In particular, a new trend to combine advanced magnetic sensors such as security sensors and data tablets with personal computers and other computer equipment, is worth noting. Such "information sensors" are likely to have a large market. This article explains the principles and construction of magnetic sensors and the evaluation of magnetic sensor materials, and summarizes topics in amorphous magnetic sensors.

articleTitle: Magnetoresistance of Multilayers
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Very large magnetoresistance (MR) effects, caused by spin-dependent electron scattering, have been found in magnetic multilayer films. The resistivity increases remarkably in cases where the magnetization of adjacent layers are antiparallel. Antiparallel magnetization may result from antiferromagnetic interlayer coupling or from differences in coercive fields. Experimental results on the MR properties of multilayer films are surveyed.

articleTitle: Exchange Coupled Films for Magnetooptic Recording Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetic properties of exchange-coupled films are discussed from the viewpoint of applications in magnetooptic recording. Various magnetic properties, such as the magnetization process, coercive force, spin orientation and Curie temperature, can be controlled through the exchange coupling. The most important and useful application involves control of the temperature dependence of the coercive force in rare earth-transition metal amorphous films. Highly controlled thermomagnetic responses bring high performance as well as new functions to magnetooptic recording media. High recording sensitivity, overwriting capability and super-high magnetic resolution all become possible through the use of exchange-coupled multilayer films. Exchange-coupled films are also expected to be prime candidates for use in future magnetooptic recording systems employing blue-light lasers.
